title: Democracy and Citizenship
summary: What democracy is, the features of South Africa's constitutional democracy, elections and the IEC, ways citizens can participate, and responsible citizenship and volunteering.

notes.text: A system of government in which power belongs to the people, who choose their leaders in free and fair elections. The word comes from Greek: *demos* (people) and *kratos* (rule).
South Africa became a **constitutional democracy** in **1994**. This means the Constitution is the highest law, and even the government must obey it.

items: **Free and fair elections** held regularly; every citizen aged **18 and older** may vote.
**Multi-party system**: people can form and join political parties.
**Human rights** are protected by a Bill of Rights.
**Separation of powers** between the legislature, executive and judiciary.
**Independent courts** and the **rule of law**: everyone, including leaders, is equal before the law.
**Accountability and transparency**: leaders must explain their actions to the people.

notes.text: The **Independent Electoral Commission (IEC)** runs national, provincial and local (municipal) elections and makes sure they are free and fair. To vote, you must be a South African citizen aged 18 or older, be **registered** on the voters' roll and have a valid ID. You can register from age **16**, and then you are ready to vote when you turn 18.

rows: Members of Parliament (the National Assembly elects the President) and provincial legislatures
Writing to a ward councillor about potholes
Attending ward committee meetings or commenting on draft laws
Signing a petition or marching for safer schools
Representative Council of Learners (RCL), youth clubs, NGOs
Helping at a soup kitchen, cleaning up a park, tutoring younger learners

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Protest is a right, but it must be **peaceful and unarmed** (section 17 of the Constitution). Burning schools, clinics or libraries harms the community and is a crime.

Good citizens obey the law, pay for services, respect others' rights, look after public property and the environment, stay informed and take part in community life. The **Representative Council of Learners (RCL)** gives learners a democratic voice in school governance.
